[[File:Certified dominating set.svg|thumb|A graph with a minimum '''certified dominating set''' colored. Red vertices are '''illuminated''', while blue vertices are '''shadowed'''.]]
In [[graph theory]], a '''certified dominating set''' of a [[Graph (discrete mathematics)|graph]] is a type of [[dominating set]] in which every vertex in the set has either zero or at least two [[neighborhood (graph theory)|neighbours]] outside the set. The concept was introduced by Dettlaff, Lemańska, Topp, Ziemann, and Żyliński in 2018.<ref name="dettlaff2020">{{cite journal |last1=Dettlaff |first1=Magda |last2=Lemańska |first2=Magdalena |last3=Topp |first3=Jerzy |last4=Ziemann |first4=Radosław |last5=Żyliński |first5=Paweł |title=Certified domination |journal=AKCE International Journal of Graphs and Combinatorics |volume=17 |issue=1 |pages=86–97 |year=2020 |doi=10.1016/j.akcej.2018.09.004 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

The concept models a scenario involving officials and civilians in a social network. Given a set <math>D</math> of officials and a set <math>W</math> of civilians, each civilian must be served by some official, and whenever an official serves a civilian, there must be at least one other civilian who can observe the official, acting as a witness to prevent potential abuse. The certified domination number represents the minimum number of officials needed to guarantee such a service.<ref name="dettlaff2020" />

== Definition ==

Let <math>G = (V, E)</math> be a graph. A [[dominating set]] <math>D \subseteq V</math> is called a '''certified dominating set''' if for every vertex <math>v \in D</math>, the number of neighbours of <math>v</math> in <math>V \setminus D</math> is either zero or at least two. Equivalently, no vertex in <math>D</math> has exactly one neighbour outside <math>D</math>.<ref name="dettlaff2020" />

The '''certified domination number''' of <math>G</math>, denoted <math>\gamma_{\text{cer}}(G)</math>, is the minimum cardinality of a certified dominating set in <math>G</math>. A certified dominating set of minimum cardinality is called a <math>\gamma_{\text{cer}}</math>'''-set'''.<ref name="dettlaff2020" /><ref name="dettlaff2019">{{cite journal |last1=Dettlaff |first1=Magda |last2=Lemańska |first2=Magdalena |last3=Miotk |first3=Mateusz |last4=Topp |first4=Jerzy |last5=Ziemann |first5=Radosław |last6=Żyliński |first6=Paweł |title=Graphs with equal domination and certified domination numbers |journal=[[Opuscula Mathematica]] |volume=39 |issue=6 |pages=815–827 |year=2019 |doi=10.7494/OpMath.2019.39.6.815 |doi-access=free|arxiv=1710.02059 }}</ref>

The vertices of <math>D</math> can be classified based on their neighbours in <math>V \setminus D</math>. A vertex in <math>D</math> with no neighbours in <math>V \setminus D</math> is called '''shadowed''', a vertex in <math>D</math> with exactly one neighbour in <math>V \setminus D</math> is called '''half-shadowed''', and a vertex in <math>D</math> with at least two neighbours in <math>V \setminus D</math> is called '''illuminated'''. A dominating set is certified if and only if it contains no half-shadowed vertices.<ref name="dettlaff2020" />

== Properties and examples ==

For any graph <math>G</math> of order <math>n</math>:<ref name="dettlaff2020" />

* The vertex set <math>V</math> is always a certified dominating set, so <math>1 \leq \gamma_{\text{cer}}(G) \leq n</math>.
* <math>\gamma_{\text{cer}}(G) \neq n - 1</math> for any graph.
* Every [[Support vertex|support vertex]] of <math>G</math> belongs to every certified dominating set.
* <math>\gamma_{\text{cer}}(G) = 1</math> if and only if <math>G</math> has order at least three and contains a [[Universal vertex|universal vertex]].
* If <math>G_1, G_2, \ldots, G_k</math> are the [[Connected component (graph theory)|connected components]] of <math>G</math>, then <math>\gamma_{\text{cer}}(G) = \sum_{i=1}^{k} \gamma_{\text{cer}}(G_i)</math>.

The certified domination number is known exactly for several families of graphs:<ref name="dettlaff2020" />

* For the [[path graph|path]] <math>P_n</math>: 
**<math>\gamma_{\text{cer}}(P_n) = 1</math> if <math>n = 1</math> or <math>n = 3</math>
**<math>\gamma_{\text{cer}}(P_n) = 2</math> if <math>n = 2</math>
**<math>\gamma_{\text{cer}}(P_n) = 4</math> if <math>n = 4</math>
**<math>\gamma_{\text{cer}}(P_n) = \lceil n/3 \rceil</math> otherwise
* For the [[cycle graph|cycle]] <math>C_n</math> with <math>n \geq 3</math>: 
**<math>\gamma_{\text{cer}}(C_n) = \lceil n/3 \rceil</math>
* For the [[complete graph]] <math>K_n</math>: 
**<math>\gamma_{\text{cer}}(K_n) = 1</math> if <math>n = 1</math> or <math>n \geq 3</math>
**<math>\gamma_{\text{cer}}(K_n) = 2</math> if <math>n = 2</math>
* For the [[complete bipartite graph]] <math>K_{m,n}</math> with <math>1 \leq m \leq n</math>: 
**<math>\gamma_{\text{cer}}(K_{m,n}) = 1</math> if <math>m = 1</math> and <math>n > 1</math>
**<math>\gamma_{\text{cer}}(K_{m,n}) = 2</math> otherwise
* For the [[wheel graph]] <math>W_n</math>: 
**<math>\gamma_{\text{cer}}(W_n) = 1</math>

=== Bounds and relation to domination number ===

Since every certified dominating set is a dominating set, <math>\gamma(G) \leq \gamma_{\text{cer}}(G)</math> for all graphs <math>G</math>. For a connected graph <math>G</math>, the certified domination number satisfies:<ref name="dettlaff2020" />

:<math>\gamma_{\text{cer}}(G) \leq \gamma(G) + |S_1(G)|</math>

where <math>\gamma(G)</math> is the [[domination number]] and <math>S_1(G)</math> is the set of weak support vertices (support vertices adjacent to exactly one [[Leaf (graph theory)|leaf]]). This bound is sharp, as equality holds for the [[Corona product|corona]] of any graph without isolated vertices. As a consequence, <math>\gamma_{\text{cer}}(G) \leq 2\gamma(G)</math>. Additionally, if the strong support vertices of <math>G</math> are adjacent to <math>k</math> leaves in total, then <math>\gamma_{\text{cer}}(G) \leq n - k</math>.<ref name="dettlaff2020" />

Equality <math>\gamma_{\text{cer}}(G) = \gamma(G)</math> holds in several cases:<ref name="dettlaff2020" /><ref name="dettlaff2019" />

* If <math>G</math> has no weak support vertex (in particular, if <math>\delta(G) \geq 2</math>), then <math>\gamma_{\text{cer}}(G) = \gamma(G)</math>.
* If <math>G</math> has a unique minimum dominating set, then <math>\gamma_{\text{cer}}(G) = \gamma(G)</math>.
* If <math>\gamma(G - v) \geq \gamma(G)</math> for every vertex <math>v</math> belonging to at least one <math>\gamma</math>-set of <math>G</math>, then <math>\gamma_{\text{cer}}(G) = \gamma(G)</math>.
* If <math>G</math> is a connected [[P4-free graph|<math>P_4</math>-free graph]] and <math>G \neq K_2</math>, then <math>\gamma_{\text{cer}}(G) = \gamma(G)</math>.

More generally, for a connected graph <math>G</math> of order at least three, <math>\gamma_{\text{cer}}(G) = \gamma(G)</math> if and only if <math>G</math> has a <math>\gamma</math>-set <math>D</math> such that every vertex in <math>D</math> has at least two neighbours in <math>V \setminus D</math>.<ref name="dettlaff2019" />

A graph <math>G</math> is called '''<math>\gamma\gamma_{\text{cer}}</math>-perfect''' if <math>\gamma(H) = \gamma_{\text{cer}}(H)</math> for every induced connected subgraph <math>H \neq K_2</math> of <math>G</math>. A graph is <math>\gamma\gamma_{\text{cer}}</math>-perfect if and only if it is <math>P_4</math>-free.<ref name="dettlaff2019" />

=== Graphs with large certified domination number ===
[[File:Certified dominating all shadow.svg|thumb|upright=0.7|The minimum certified dominating set for the graph shown consists of the entire vertex set]]

A graph <math>G</math> of order <math>n</math> satisfies <math>\gamma_{\text{cer}}(G) = n</math> if and only if <math>G</math> is the [[complement (graph theory)|complement]] of a [[complete graph]], the [[corona product|corona]] of a graph, or the disjoint union of both.<ref name="dettlaff2020" />

A '''diadem graph''' is a graph obtained from the corona <math>H \circ K_1</math> by adding a new vertex and joining it to one support vertex of <math>H \circ K_1</math>. A graph <math>G</math> of order <math>n \geq 3</math> satisfies <math>\gamma_{\text{cer}}(G) = n - 2</math> if and only if <math>G</math> is <math>C_3</math>, <math>C_4</math>, or a diadem graph, possibly combined with the corona of a graph and isolated vertices.<ref name="dettlaff2020" />

=== Effects of graph modifications ===

Adding an edge to a [[connected graph]] cannot increase the certified domination number: <math>\gamma_{\text{cer}}(G + e) \leq \gamma_{\text{cer}}(G)</math>. However, both deleting an edge from a graph and adding an edge to a disconnected graph may arbitrarily increase the certified domination number.<ref name="dettlaff2020" />

Adding a leaf vertex may arbitrarily increase the certified domination number, but adding a non-leaf vertex <math>v</math> to a graph <math>G</math> satisfies <math>\gamma_{\text{cer}}(G + v) \leq \gamma_{\text{cer}}(G) + 1</math>.<ref name="dettlaff2020" />

=== Nordhaus–Gaddum type inequalities ===

For a graph <math>G</math> of order <math>n \geq 5</math> with [[complement (graph theory)|complement]] <math>\overline{G}</math>:<ref name="dettlaff2020" />

:<math>\gamma_{\text{cer}}(G) + \gamma_{\text{cer}}(\overline{G}) \leq n + 2</math>
:<math>\gamma_{\text{cer}}(G) \cdot \gamma_{\text{cer}}(\overline{G}) \leq 2n</math>

Equality holds in both inequalities simultaneously if and only if <math>G</math> or <math>\overline{G}</math> is the corona of some graph.<ref name="dettlaff2020" />

If <math>\min\{\delta(G), \delta(\overline{G})\} \geq 2</math>, stronger bounds hold:<ref name="dettlaff2020" />

:<math>\gamma_{\text{cer}}(G) + \gamma_{\text{cer}}(\overline{G}) \leq \left\lfloor \frac{n}{2} \right\rfloor + 2</math>
:<math>\gamma_{\text{cer}}(G) \cdot \gamma_{\text{cer}}(\overline{G}) \leq n</math>

== Computational complexity ==

The problem of determining the certified domination number is [[NP-hard]] even for [[bipartite graph|bipartite]] [[planar graph|planar]] subcubic graphs with no leaves. This follows from the equality <math>\gamma_{\text{cer}}(G) = \gamma(G)</math> for graphs with no weak support vertices and the known NP-hardness of the domination problem in such graph classes.<ref name="dettlaff2020" />

Determining whether <math>\gamma(G) \neq \gamma_{\text{cer}}(G)</math> for a given graph <math>G</math> is also NP-hard, even when <math>G</math> has only one weak support vertex. This is shown by a reduction from [[Boolean satisfiability problem#3-satisfiability|3SAT]].<ref name="raczek2025">{{cite journal |last1=Raczek |first1=Joanna |last2=Miotk |first2=Mateusz |title=Two Approaches to Constructing Certified Dominating Sets in Social Networks |journal=[[IEEE Access]] |volume=13 |pages=17495–17505 |year=2025 |doi=10.1109/ACCESS.2025.3532392 |doi-access=free}}</ref>
